top_cited_works.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics Modeling of Combustor Performance in the ARC-S1 Gas Turbine Combustor
top_cited_works.abstract: The internal dynamics of liquid-fueled gas turbine combustors are complex due to the interaction between the spray physics, turbulence, and combustion. Computational tools help understand these processes. A Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) model is developed for the Army Research Combustor-small size, ARC-S1 to characterize the steady-state combustion behavior of F-24 jet fuel for different operating conditions and geometry. High quality droplet data, measured with high-speed X-ray phase contrast imaging, is used for spray model initialization. The initial design of ARC-S1 is based on a trapped vortex cavity combustor. To compare changes in the geometry, metrics such as the mass exchange between cavities, fuel consumption, and combustion efficiency are developed. In particular, the impact of swirl and cavity shapes are investigated for a range of operating conditions. In general, it is observed that the presence of swirl can improve mixing but also increases fuel lost as film on the walls of the cavities and combustor. Modification in the cavity geometry can lead to changes in temperature distribution that can be leveraged for improved fuel consumption.

top_cited_works.title: Combustion Characteristics in an Ultra-Compact Trapped Vortex Combustor with Liquid Fuel Sprays
top_cited_works.abstract: In the design of small-scale power generation systems using a combustor, achievement of high-efficiency, stable operation, and size reduction are critical challenges. To address these issues, studies on the concept and design of small-size combustors and their combustion characteristics are highly desirable. In this study, a small-scale trapped vortex combustor with fuel atomizing sprays is designed and combustion characteristics is experimentally studied. Visible and OH* chemiluminescence imaging are performed to visually inspect the flame and observe the spatial distribution of the primary chemical reaction region. Because the atomization and vaporization of the liquid fuel are critical to the combustion performance, qualitative and quantitative investigation of fuel sprays are conducted using X-ray phase contrast imaging. Combustion efficiency measurement is performed to examine the combustion performance. Combustion characteristics in the combustor are discussed with obtained spray information, heat release zone images, and combustion efficiencies. top_cited_works.title: Effects of pilot fraction and dwell time on ignition performance of an IPK fuel
top_cited_works.abstract: This study experimentally investigates the effects of pilot fraction (the ratio of pilot to total fuel quantity) and dwell time (the interval between pilot and main injections) on ignition behavior of an Isoparaffinic Kerosene (IPK) fuel. Simultaneous chemiluminescence and schlieren imaging were employed in a constant-flow chamber at three ambient conditions representing low to medium loads in compression-ignition engines. Ignition performance was evaluated using the integrated chemiluminescence intensity obtained from each condition, with the optimal case defined as the condition yielding the maximum overall intensity. Results indicate that the optimal pilot fraction remains consistent at an intermediate value across all conditions: a small pilot mass rapidly leans out, reducing its contribution to main-injection ignition, while a large pilot mass penetrates excessively, limiting its interaction with the main injection. recent_works.title: Pilot Injection Impact on Ignition of F-24/ATJ Blends Under Various Conditions
recent_works.abstract: This study experimentally investigates the effects of pilot injection on ignition performance for blends of conventional petroleum-derived aviation fuel (F-24) and an isobutanol-derived alcohol-to-jet (ATJ) fuel. The fuel blends are injected into a constant flow combustion chamber under various thermodynamic conditions to simulate the ignition process in compression-ignition (CI) engines. Simultaneous imaging of planar laser-induced fluorescence of formaldehyde, chemiluminescence, and schlieren are performed to analyze the detailed ignition process. Variations in fuel blend, ambient conditions, and injection strategies yield distinct ignition behaviors. Blends with higher ratios of ATJ and lower thermodynamic conditions reduce overall heat release and increase both first stage and overall ignition delays, occasionally leading to misfire. Compared to a single injection, the addition of a pilot injection to the main injection enhances overall heat release and reduces both first stage and overall ignition delays across all fuel blends and ambient conditions. This acceleration of the ignition process results from early formation of intermediate combustion radicals from the pilot mix...
